atoms.b:
The generation gap
Every generation tends to believe that its values and experiences are unique. ((In_fact)), there have always been tensions between older and younger generations.

Baby Boomers, ((for_instance)), often criticise younger people for being too dependent on technology, ((while)) Generation Z argues that older generations fail to understand the realities of the modern world.
((Even_though)) both sides have valid points, the generation gap can lead to misunderstandings.
Older generations ((generally)) value stability, hard work, and face-to-face communication.
Younger people, ((on_the_other_hand)), tend to prioritise flexibility, digital literacy, and a healthy work-life balance.
((Despite)) these differences, studies show that all generations share core values ((such_as)) honesty, fairness, and the desire for a better future.
((In_short)), the so-called generation gap may not be as wide as it seems.

atoms.b: ((In_fact)), much of the conflict stems from communication styles rather than fundamental disagreements.
